fixes.explanation: Nations is a big word, friend. But the verse never says anything about nations. Jesus gave the Twelve "…power and authority over all demons…" (Luke 9:1). It's a different kind of authority, and it's the one the text names.
The law of Moses is a big name, friend, but Luke 9:2 says they were sent "…to proclaim the kingdom of God…" The law of Moses isn't what the verse names as their message. The message is the kingdom.
Three nights at most is a very specific number, friend. But Jesus never gives a count of nights. He says to stay in the house "…until you leave that area." (Luke 9:4).

Yes, baker. Jesus says, "…shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town, as a testimony against them." (Luke 9:5). That's the instruction for a town that doesn't welcome them. The dust comes off their feet as they leave.
Tearing cloaks is a dramatic move, friend, but Jesus never says it here. His instruction is, "…shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town…" (Luke 9:5). That's the action He names.
Jerusalem is a big destination, friend, but this verse doesn't send them there. Luke 9:6 says they "…went from village to village…" That's how the text describes their travel.

Pleased isn't what the verse says, friend. When Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, he "was perplexed" (Luke 9:7). Perplexed means puzzled, like staring at a recipe with half the words missing.

Right, baker. Luke 9:8 says others were saying "…Elijah had appeared…" People were tossing several names into the mix. Some said John had risen from the dead, and still others said a prophet of old had arisen (Luke 9:7–8).
Moses is a big name, friend, but he isn't the one in this verse. Luke 9:8 says others were saying "…Elijah had appeared…" Moses isn't named in these rumors.
Samuel is a good guess, friend. But Luke 9:8 names someone else. It says others were saying "…Elijah had appeared…"

Yes, baker. Herod says, "I beheaded John," and then asks, "…but who is this man I hear such things about?" (Luke 9:9). He's got a pile of rumors and not one clear answer. The text adds that he kept trying to see Jesus.
